doc.title: Eddie Miller and Pete Fountain Interview, 1970-01-09

chapter: Callers, Bourbon Street and big bands
title: Doc Severinsen expected at the club
summary: Pete and Ramsey talk about Doc Severinsen sitting in, his transformation, and Ed McMahon.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: Thank you, sir. Thanks for your call, sir. Thanks. Good stuff. What do you think is going to happen when Doc Severinsen walks in tonight? Does he bring his horn?

Well, we have a horn ready for him if he don't, because he loves to play. The last time he was in town, he worked. He sat there all night. He did a concert here, and the next thing you know, he did two shows with us. He just sat up on the stand. He says, I'm safe to her up there, which is true. Musicians feel a lot better. My work isn't on the stand. It's off the stand, you know, really. Not to get through the crowd or autograph, but you feel like you're more relaxed upon to stand with the clarinet in your mouth.

You know, Doc's from Portland, where I worked before I came here. Did you know him there? Yeah, I knew him, and I knew his dad. His dad is a dentist out there. Watching Doc on the Tonight Show these days is kind of amazing. He's undergone a complete transformation. He used to wear, you know, like 1945-style double-breasted suits and Army shoes. He's on a complete other way. And now he's one of the world's best-dressed men.

He and his wife are just two great people. I think she's coming on with him. Good. And Ed McMahon, too. Yeah, Big Ed will be here with the... You're well-stocked over there. ...sapenade. Carries a sapenade with the jug around his back.
